verdicts.note: The pole_a evidence is one 2025 floor speech ('finally fund the police', tougher theft and fentanyl penalties) [S20] and a website promise of 'safer streets' [S2]. The same speech pairs penalties with more treatment facilities [S20], and she voted against ESHB 2015, the 2025 public-safety funding bill for officer hiring and co-response [S13] (its local option tax is the likely reason, but the record cuts against a full 'fund the police' placement). Clear lean toward enforcement, not the full pole.

Her only statement places her 'kind of in the middle' on data centers, 'listening and learning', wanting more study and legislation 'so that it benefits our communities' [S15]. The nay on E2SHB 2515 [S14] points toward pole_a, but against her own stated middle position the direction is inferential; low confidence.
The SSB 5917 nay [S12] is direct reproductive-policy record; 'defend family values' [S1] adds little. One vote, so -1 medium rather than -2.

The source quote is mixed: 'the most obvious is trying to find ways to relieve taxes off of working people. I think the millionaire's tax is a great path forward, though it's worrisome that there isn't language in there that it won't affect working people' [S5]; she also withdrew support for the 2025 gas tax [S5]. Support for the millionaire's tax points to pole_b, but there is no call to expand progressive revenue beyond it, so +1.

Website: will 'prevent state and local resources from being used for federal immigration enforcement' and protect families 'from ICE overreach' [S2]; consistent with her worker-protection plank. Explicit and repeated.
'I am completely against data centers' and wants 'a ban in place for data centers' until regulations exist [S4]. One interview, so medium is right.
